title: Strong as death (Song of Songs 8:6–7)
hookLine: "love is strong as death... Many waters cannot quench love"

lines: A FIRE THE FLOODS CAN'T PUT OUT.
AS STRONG AS WHAT NOBODY ESCAPES.
cards: "Many waters cannot quench love, Neither can the floods drown it." Floods are an old picture of a force nothing stops. In Genesis the waters rise until the mountains are covered.
Here, near the end of the Song of Songs, the waters meet something they can't put out.
The woman in the Song asks her beloved to keep her close, and then tells him why: love holds on as hard as the one thing nobody escapes.

teach.h: SET ME AS A SEAL UPON THY HEART.

teach.b: The verse just before, in the JPS 1917 translation: "Set me as a seal upon thy heart, As a seal upon thine arm; For love is strong as death, Jealousy is cruel as the grave; The flashes thereof are flashes of fire, A very flame of the LORD."

A seal is a mark that says whose something is. Set me as a seal: wear me where you can't forget me, on your heart and on your arm. In Hebrew the line runs azzah khamavet ahavah: strong as death, love.
Death doesn't give back what it takes. The Song says love holds on just as hard. Not gentler than death.
Then the flame. The verse's last Hebrew word is shalhevetyah, and its last syllable, yah, is also a short form of God's name. The JPS translators heard it that way: a very flame of the LORD.
Others take the yah as a way of saying a mighty flame. The text lets it flicker both ways. Then the floods.
Water puts out fire; that's what water does. Except this fire. And the verse closes with a warning: "If a man would give all the substance of his house for love, He would utterly be contemned."
Love can't be bought. It can only be kept burning. And notice what the Song doesn't claim.
It doesn't call love gentle, or easy, or safe; in the same breath it says jealousy is cruel as the grave. It calls love strong.

how: Jewish tradition reads the Song of Songs as love between God and Israel as well as between people, and some couples use the words 'set me as a seal upon thy heart' at their weddings.

games.q: you're the woman in the Song, and your beloved is going away for a while. what do you ask for?
o: set me as a seal upon thy heart.
a gift worth all his house.
games.why: she asks to be worn like a seal on his heart and arm, 'for love is strong as death.'

practice: Bring to mind a love that has been tested, by distance, by time, by a hard season, maybe by a death; it might be someone still here, or someone you still love who is gone.
Rest a hand on your heart, where the Song asks to be worn like a seal, and hold that person there for a few slow breaths, asking nothing of the memory. If you pray, you can hold them in your prayers.

wordCard.voice: Azzah. Hebrew for strong: the Song's claim that love holds on as hard as death does, and many waters cannot quench it. Today's word.
